title: Down 98%, Is it Finally Time to Buy Chargepoint Stock? | CHPT Stock Analysis
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc revisits ChargePoint after a fall of more than 98% over five years and asks whether it is finally time to buy, against a backdrop of higher oil prices and faster EV adoption outside the United States (he notes the US is only 6 of 100 new EV buyers). The operating story has genuinely improved: revenue is recovering to $433 million on a trailing basis with another growth quarter forecast, management has stopped growing at any cost, the latest quarter was essentially cash-flat, and operating cash flow relative to sales has improved from minus 65% to minus 16%. The balance sheet is the problem: cash has dwindled from over $600 million to just over $95 million against more than $227 million of debt — more than the market capitalisation — so any return to the old burn rate would force dilutive raises or expensive borrowing. His discounted cash flow, which only reaches free-cash-flow break-even in fiscal 2028 and positive territory from fiscal 2029, still leaves the stock overvalued at the stated $8 price (up 11% on the day) even after a margin of safety; the fair-value figure itself is garbled in the auto-captions, rendered as '$529' where $5.29 fits the pattern of dropped decimals. The call is CHPT — AVOID, reiterating a warning he has given for over five years, though he says it is getting closer.

calls.thesis: AVOID, first tracked Parkevtate CHPT call (no flip) — he reiterates a warning he has given for 5+ years and last on 15 Jun: ChargePoint is still not a buying opportunity even after falling over 98%, though it is getting closer. He has never ranked it a buy.
calls.base_case: Revenue is recovering ($433m trailing 12 months, with another growth quarter forecast) after management stopped growth-at-any-cost and fixed unit economics; the latest quarter was essentially cash-flat, and operating cash flow/sales improved from -65% to -16% on a trailing basis.
calls.bull_case: If ChargePoint can stay cash-flat until revenue growth accelerates into positive free cash flow (his DCF: free-cash-flow break-even in fiscal 2028, positive from fiscal 2029), it avoids further dilutive raises; persistently higher oil prices and faster EV adoption outside the US (Europe, China, South-East Asia; the US is only 6 of 100 new buyers) support charging demand.
calls.bear_case: Cash has dwindled from over $600m to just over $95m against over $227m of debt — more than the market capitalisation; a return to historic burn rates would force dilutive raises or desperate, high-rate borrowing, and even after a margin of safety his DCF still leaves the stock overvalued at $8.
